collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: An outsider offers a fortune for a healer's medicine knowledge: share it, or keep it in the village.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A visitor has offered (subject) a canoe full of goods for the secret of the medicine garden: which plant cures which ailment. (subject) thinks the knowledge could help sick people on other islands. (friend), who taught (subject.him/her), says the knowledge belongs to the village, not to one healer. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) brings it to the village. They agree to share some of it, on condition that the visitor teaches the healers what (other.his/her) island knows in return. The visitor agrees. Both islands' healers learn something.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) refuses. The visitor leaves disappointed. (friend) is proud of (subject.him/her). Months later, a sick child from the visitor's island is brought to Isola for treatment, and (subject) treats (other.him/her) without asking for anything.
